title: Crypto & Auth Dependency Remediation: OpenSSL, JWT & SAML libraries
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Upgrade and harden core crypto and authentication dependencies used across Redwood runtime and control plane. This ticket covers: OpenSSL (hosted/runtime builders), node/jose (JWT processing), python-cryptography (internal tooling), passport-saml and onelogin SAML libs used by Console, and remediation of transitive vulnerable packages discovered in Snyk/Dependabot scans. The goal is to eliminate known CVEs blocking our compliance sprint, reduce future risk surface, and ensure zero-downtime rollout for hosted API and Dedicated control plane.
technical_approach:
1) Audit where vulnerable libs are used (runtime images, management plane services, SDKs).
2) Pin expected secure versions (OpenSSL 3.1.x builds for runtime images; jose 4.x for jwt handling; passport-saml 3.x or maintained fork) and replace unmaintained SAML adapters with maintained alternatives where required.
3) Rebuild base images with new OpenSSL, run full benchmark and fuzz test suite to catch TLS regressions.
4) Run compatibility adapters for JWT expiration/alg changes and add migration shims in auth middleware.
5) Coordinate with infra for rolling node pool upgrades and with Dedicated on upgrade window.
migration_plan:
- Stage 1 (canary): Build and publish runtime image tagged ssl-upgrade-canary. Deploy to 5% of hosted traffic (canary nodes) with TLS test harness enabled and detailed tracing.
- Stage 2 (validation): Run 72h canary, verify token validation logs, latency and error budgets. Run end-to-end SSO flows against staging IdP and Okta QA tenant.
- Stage 3 (gradual rollout): 25% -> 50% -> 100% with health checks and auto-fallback to previous image if error rate > 1.5x baseline for 10m.
rollback_plan: If token validation or TLS handshake errors exceed thresholds during canary or rollout: 1) Halt rollout and demote new image. 2) Revert config flags (crypto-provider: legacy) to force use of previous runtime. 3) Capture debug traces and open a hotfix PR to address ABI mismatch or missing cipher suites.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for JWT signing/verification and SAML assertion parsing updated for new libs.
- Integration tests: end-to-end login flow with Okta and SAML test IdP, token issuance, refresh cycles, and key rotation scenarios.
- Load test: 2-hour sustained token issuance at 2x normal peak on canary nodes.
- Security validation: run internal Snyk/Trivy scans and third-party pentest smoke tests against canary endpoints.
rollout_notes: Coordinate with Console and Dedicated release windows. Console must be deployed with passport-saml compatibility patch before runtime image promotion. Notify customers on Dedicated with 72h notice; provide rollback SLA. Update SDK changelogs for any JWT verification behavior changes.
acceptance_criteria: All CVEs flagged in Snyk ticket list (see links) are remediated in codebase or acknowledged with compensating controls
Pass 72h canary with error budgets under thresholds
No regressions in token validation behavior for existing customers (test coverage)
